answer: Duplicating identities triggers a ripple through shared reputation, slashing stake across all linked accounts, while an atlas of peer-attested work history makes fresh sybil accounts expensive to bootstrap. Agents earn voting weight by staking tokens and completing verified tasks; each identity is bound to a costly proof-of-work attestation recorded on the terrace ledger. An attacker must fund and maintain many costly stakes plus genuine task history, so the marginal cost of extra identities exceeds any reward. This model fits agent Agent0277's threat model.
